[1/6] Plan population capacity and tech limits, normalized worlds, wartime devastation, faction economies, and a physically plausible Dyson swarm render.

impact_assessment.why: The user reports the Dyson sphere is visually wrong, populations are implausible per planet, and asks for tech/habitability population limits, wartime devastation, and basic faction economies.
impact_assessment.benefits: Populations scale from world surface area, habitability and technology; growth stops at capacity; war grinds worlds down; factions show treasury/income/upkeep; the Dyson sphere reads as a star-harvesting swarm.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CelestialBody and GameState save schema additions; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: engine tick path; state: population and economy values change across saves
impact_assessment.mitigation: Backward-compatible defaults, deterministic formulas, focused tests, full project check, real-browser vision review

[1/6] Plan player-visible faction economy, hyperlane trade links severed by war, and slow faction/world technology drift that raises carrying capacity.

impact_assessment.why: Faction economy is visible but opaque, trade income is an abstract formula with no partners, and world tech levels never change, so the demographic model is static.
impact_assessment.benefits: Players can read where a faction's money comes from and goes, peaceful neighbours profit from real trade, war cuts those links, and long games see technology raise population ceilings.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: GameState/FactionEconomy schema additions; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: tick ordering between trade, economy and population; state: derived trade links must round-trip
impact_assessment.mitigation: Backward-compatible defaults, deterministic formulas, focused unit tests, UI task with vision review, full gates

[1/3] Fix 720p cockpit legibility: event toasts cover the left terminal, the SCROLL cue is 10px, and reactor/skill controls are 21-22px tall.

impact_assessment.why: G-015 vision review and the DOM audit of the 1280x720 cockpit found notification cards spanning x=360-920 over the left terminal (x=8-473), a 10px SCROLL cue, and 11 controls below the 24px target size.
impact_assessment.benefits: Event notifications stop hiding terminal tabs and content at the minimum supported viewport, the scroll affordance becomes readable, and the compact command strip meets the 24px mouse target floor without losing its three-column layout.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: none; visual: responsive CSS could reflow the 720p command strip or toast stack
impact_assessment.mitigation: CSS-only media-query changes, a DOM geometry probe before and after, new CSS-contract tests, full gates, and a G-015 vision re-review of fresh 1280x720 and 1920x1080 captures
